title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Audio-Visual Gaze Control

fields.value: Technical/system description with offline dataset and simulation evaluation, plus live experiments on a robot.

quotes.text: We introduce a simulated environment that enables us to learn the proposed deep RL model without the need of spending hours of tedious interaction.
By experimenting on a publicly available dataset and on a real robot, we provide empirical evidence that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance.
In order to carry out an online evaluation of our method, we performed experiments with a Nao robot.

fields.value: Audio-visual gaze control: combining controlled robot motion with acoustic and visual observations to direct the robot head toward groups of people.

quotes.text: In this paper, we address the problem of audio-visual gaze control, or more precisely, how a robot should combine controlled motions with acoustic and visual observations in order to direct its head towards groups of people.

fields.value: The authors describe gaze control as selecting head motions using audio-visual observations to direct the robot toward people; the stated objective is to maximize visible people and possibly favor those engaged in speech.

quotes.text: The objective is to design a methodology that enables robots to learn gazing strategies from data; for example, to maximize the number of persons that are present in its visual field of view and, possibly, to favor people engaged in spoken communication.
The desired robot action is to rotate its head, on which are mounted a camera and two microphones, such as to maximize the number of persons visible in the camera field-of-view.

fields.value: Gaze control maintains people in the robot’s visual and acoustic fields of view so it can receive instructions and favor speaking participants; it supports group awareness and information gathering.

quotes.text: In situations such as the ones cited, a robot teammate must constantly maintain the participants in its visual and acoustic fields of view such that it can easily receive instructions while respecting social etiquette.
In multi-party scenarios, focusing on only one person may lead to miss important information such as who looks at whom and who is the speaker and who are the listeners [1].

fields.value: The system’s reported effects are on technical performance: audio-visual fusion and reinforcement learning improved gaze-control rewards relative to unimodal or handcrafted approaches. No measured effects on participants are reported.

fields.value: Autonomous deep Q-learning with an LSTM-based Q-function; inputs are motor positions, visual landmark grids and audio speech-source grids. Actions rotate the head left, right, up, down, or stay still. Training used simulation and the learned model was transferred to Nao.

quotes.text: A motor action At (rotate left, right, up, down, or stay still) is selected based on past and present observations via maximization of current and future rewards.

fields.value: This paper presents an autonomous deep reinforcement learning system that controls a Nao robot’s audio-visual gaze in group scenarios, aiming to keep people visible and favor speakers. In dataset, simulation, and live robot evaluations, audio-visual fusion performed well, and the learned policy outperformed handcrafted strategies under equal movement limits.

RQ1; RQ2; RQ4; RQ5; RQ6 — The paper states its gaze-control framing and purpose in group interaction, describes the sensing, learning, and control implementation, and specifies the Nao embodiment and how its acoustic properties shaped sensing. It does not report participant-level effects or enough participant/session details to answer RQ3.
